claim: v7a is an ELF32 ARM little-endian ET_DYN shared object whose first PT_LOAD is at vaddr 0 (module-relative address == vaddr), p_align 0x1000.
location: v7a ELF header + program headers (analysis/native/elf_audit.v7a.json: header, segments)
observation: e_type ET_DYN, e_machine EM_ARM, e_flags 0x5000002 (EABI5, no float-ABI bits); PT_LOAD[0] vaddr 0x0 filesz 0x89b5c R E align 0x1000; PT_LOAD[1] vaddr 0x8ab5c off 0x89b5c memsz 0x321cd8 RW align 0x1000; entry 0x13ad0 (= Java_..._JNIAudioInit, irrelevant for a .so).
interpretation: Addresses in all native docs are ELF vaddrs; 4 KiB segment alignment only matters for the original .so.

claim: v7a uses the softfp float ABI: VFPv2 instructions are used internally but float arguments/returns travel in core registers.
location: v7a .ARM.attributes (elf_audit.v7a.json arm_attributes); e.g. v7a:0x1556c nativeResize (vmov s13, r5)
observation: Tag_CPU_arch v7, Tag_FP_arch VFPv2, Tag_ABI_HardFP_use 'deprecated', no Tag_ABI_VFP_args (=AAPCS base). 24,220 capstone 'vfp2'-group instructions in $a regions.
interpretation: Ghidra's default ARM.cspec prototype passes floats in s0-s15 (hard-float); the export script therefore re-applies every v7a function with ARM.cspec's __stdcall_softfp. A native arm64 port must not reuse ARM32 float-ABI assumptions anyway.

claim: Both libraries are ARM-state only (no Thumb code) as far as static evidence reaches.
location: v7a/v5 .symtab mapping symbols; capstone over all $a regions (elf_audit.*.json instruction_set_evidence)
observation: v7a: 1261 $a / 849 $d / 0 $t; 0 odd FUNC values; 107,385 instructions decoded in ARM mode with 0 invalid; 0 BLX-immediate; 3 'blx reg' (all in libgcc unwinder). v5: 1178 $a / 729 $d / 0 $t; 116,938 instructions, 0 invalid, 0 BLX-immediate.
interpretation: Indirect BX/BLX targets cannot be proven statically, but every function pointer materialised in data/GOT (EV-NAT-0024) is even.
next_step: Confirm under the Unicorn harness that no indirect branch sets the T bit.

claim: DT_TEXTREL is set, and the only text relocations are 12 inside the libgcc unwinder; game code has none.
observation: 2 R_ARM_ABS32 (__cxa_call_unexpected @0x7f540, __gnu_Unwind_Find_exidx @0x7f678) + 10 R_ARM_RELATIVE (personality table 0x7f67c-0x7f68c, _Unwind_VRS_Pop jump table 0x7faa0-0x7fab0). Relocation census: 936 RELATIVE, 94 JUMP_SLOT, 2 ABS32, 2 GLOB_DAT (__stack_chk_guard, __sF).
interpretation: The unwinder objects were built non-PIC; irrelevant for a source rebuild (the arm64 port uses its own unwinder).

claim: No JNI_OnLoad, no DT_INIT/DT_FINI/FINI_ARRAY, no dlopen/dlsym; liblog.so is NEEDED but no liblog symbol is imported.
observation: NEEDED libc.so libstdc++.so libm.so libGLESv1_CM.so libdl.so liblog.so; DT_SYMBOLIC+DT_TEXTREL set; 97 imports (92 FUNC), none named __android_log_*, dlopen, dlsym, __cxa_atexit.
interpretation: JNI binding is purely by Java_* symbol names (18 exports). No global destructors are ever registered.

claim: INIT_ARRAY has 11 R_ARM_RELATIVE entries, each resolving to a _GLOBAL__I_<file>.cpp static constructor; no 0/-1 sentinels.
observation: Targets in order: Ad.cpp 0x13b4c, RMaths.cpp 0x1822c, RShell.cpp 0x1a46c, RObject.cpp 0x1d294, Font.cpp 0x21f70, RSprite.cpp 0x2ce58, Game.cpp 0x2e190, SubGame.cpp 0x73b08, Voice.cpp 0x76f6c, LoadingBar.cpp 0x799fc, GL.cpp 0x7a858.
interpretation: The file names give the original translation units. That bionic runs them in index order before System.loadLibrary returns is likely (platform behaviour), not observed.

claim: tColour::tColour() and tColourSmall::tColourSmall() default constructors are empty, so static-ctor loops over them are no-ops.
observation: Each body is the single instruction 'bx lr' (e12fff1e).
interpretation: Only the Ad.cpp (gConfig defaults), RMaths.cpp (gUnitMatrix), RShell.cpp, Font.cpp (cRBod x128), Voice.cpp and LoadingBar.cpp constructors have observable effects.

claim: wprintf(char*, ...) is a no-op: all native logging is compiled out.
observation: push {r0-r3}; add sp, sp, #16; bx lr.
interpretation: Log strings are still in .rodata and are useful as labels, but nothing is printed at runtime.

claim: v5 is a soft-float v5TE build of the same program; its only VFP instructions are inside libgcc unwinder save/restore helpers.
observation: Tag_CPU_arch v5TE, no Tag_FP_arch. 6 capstone vfp2-group instructions (fldmiax/fstmiax/vldmia/vstmia), all in __gnu_Unwind_* helpers. 100 runtime functions incl. soft-float helpers (__addsf3, __aeabi_fmul, __divsf3, ...). Same 1096 game + 18 jni functions as v7a.
interpretation: v5 is useful as a second compilation for cross-checking semantics (different register allocation / soft-float calls), not as a primary reference.

claim: JNIDatInit opens assets/asm.mp3 through the passed FileDescriptor and loads the archive directory into gDat, indexing names in gDatHash.
observation: JNIEnv calls +0x18 FindClass('java/io/FileDescriptor'), +0x54, +0x178 GetFieldID('descriptor','I'), +0x190 GetIntField; then dup(); r3 -> gJavaAssetStart (0x1530c), [sp+0x128] -> gJavaAssetLength (0x15318); fdopen(fid,'rb') -> gDatFP; fseek(start); fread(hdr,1,0xF4); gDat = RShellMemoryMalloc(hdr[+8]); fseek; fread(gDat,1,hdr[+8]); cRHash::Init(&gDatHash, gDat[0], DatHashGetString); loop i<gDat[0]: rec=gDat+i*24, rec[+4] += gDat, cRHash::Add(&gDatHash, rec[+4], i).
interpretation: Start/length are 32-bit ints (r3 + one stack word). This is consistent with docs/JNI_MAP.json, which gives JNIDatInit as private static native (Ljava/io/FileDescriptor;II)V, so r1 is a jclass. Record-format semantics belong to the assets worker.

claim: cRHash stores a name-getter callback at this+0x808 and cRHash::Search calls it indirectly; only two callbacks exist.
location: v7a:0x7d354 (str r2,[r4,#0x808] in cRHash::Init), v7a:0x7d1dc (ldr pc,[r4,#0x808] in cRHash::Search), v7a:0x153c4, v7a:0x1c018, v7a:0x1cb58
observation: GOT-held pointers to DatHashGetString (0x19954; taken by JNIDatInit and RShellDatInit) and TexturesFunctionGetName (0x1c2b0; taken by cRTextures::Init) are the only function addresses loaded by those Init callers.
interpretation: The indirect call at 0x7d1dc resolves per-instance to one of these two functions.

claim: nativeInit caches JNI state, clears the resource manager and schedules two black frames; it does not initialise the game.
observation: bl JAVA_RegisterFunctions (0x13ca4); bl cRResourceManager::Init(&gResourceManager) (0x7e8b4); G0StartBlackCount = 2 (0x15678).
interpretation: Game construction is deferred to the per-frame AppInit state machine (EV-NAT-0018).

claim: nativeReInit re-registers JNI, re-initialises GL state, starts a resource reload, arms the auto-quit counter and schedules two black frames, dereferencing Game without a null check.
observation: bl JAVA_RegisterFunctions; bl InitGL (0x7ab84); bl cRResourceManager::ReInit (0x7ed5c); ldr r1,[Game]; str #4,[r1,#0x718b4]; G0StartBlackCount = 2.
interpretation: Called on GL context re-creation. If the managed side could call it before AppInit state 0 set Game, it would fault (hypothesis).

claim: nativeResize stores the surface size as floats in four globals and issues no GL calls.
observation: vcvt.f32.s32 of w -> gG0DeviceScreenWidth and gG0ScreenWidth; of h -> gG0ScreenHeight and gG0DeviceScreenHeight; wprintf is a no-op.
interpretation: glViewport is issued per frame by G0Render (0x7ad84) from gG0DeviceScreenWidth/Height.

claim: nativePause toggles San-Angeles-style timing statics that nothing else reads, so it has no effect on the game.
observation: Toggle sDemoStopped; if now stopped sTimeStopped=_getTime() (gettimeofday ms, 0x154c0) else sTimeOffset += sTimeStopped - _getTime(). The capstone resolver (xrefs.v7a.json) and Ghidra pseudocode both show these three statics referenced only in nativePause.
interpretation: Leftover of the Android NDK 'San Angeles' sample glue (the names importGLInit/appRender/appDeinit/_getTime match that sample; hypothesis for provenance). The effective pause path is nativeRender's third argument (EV-NAT-0039).

claim: nativeDone, JNIAudioInit, appDeinit and importGLDeinit are no-ops.
observation: JNIAudioInit/appDeinit/importGLDeinit are 'bx lr'; nativeDone = bl appDeinit; b importGLDeinit.
interpretation: No native teardown exists: gDatFP stays open and Game is never freed (there is no operator delete import).

claim: JAVA_RegisterFunctions caches env/thiz/class and resolves 26 Java callback method IDs from the gJAVAFunction table.
location: v7a:0x13ca4-0x13d78; table gJAVAFunction v7a:0x8b3f0 (12-byte records {methodID, name*, sig*})
observation: GetObjectClass (+0x7c) then GetMethodID (+0x84) for records 0..25: JAVALoadSample..JAVAVibrate; JAVATime at +0x114, JAVATimeHi at +0x120.
interpretation: Called from both nativeInit and nativeReInit, so the cached JNIEnv* is refreshed per GL thread.
next_step: JNI worker: map every method ID to ADRenderer methods (docs/JNI_MAP.json).

claim: AppInit (called every frame) is the boot state machine: two black frames, OpenFeint load/save hooks, a resource-manager gate, a loading-bar gate, then gAppState 0..10 advanced by one per frame.
location: v7a:0x1639c-0x16740; jump table v7a:0x16470 (addls pc,pc,r3,lsl #2; 11 entries at 0x16474-0x164a0)
observation: State bodies: 0 RShellInit/RMathInit/new cRGame/InitGL/cRLoadingBar::Init (0x16658); 1 cRGame::Init0 (0x166bc); 2 gRegisterLoadFile('asm.cfg', gConfig) (0x16544); 3 Init1; 4 Init2; 5 Init3; 6 Init4; 7 Init5; 8 G0TextureSetLoad(1); 9 InitLast + LoadingBar::Finish + gGameValid=1 + cRFade::StartOn (0x164ec); 10 return 1 without incrementing (0x1642c). The common exit 0x16530 increments gAppState and returns 0.
interpretation: Nothing reaches appRender until gAppState==10; boot costs at least 12 frames after nativeInit.

claim: The game object is heap-allocated once: Game = operator new(0x3a6468) followed by cRGame::cRGame().
observation: movw/movt r0 = 0x3a6468; bl _Znwj@plt (0x13a1c); bl _ZN6cRGameC1Ev (0x1605c); str r6, [Game].
interpretation: cRGame is 3,826,792 bytes. Its constructor installs 13 vtables (classes.v7a.json vtables.materialised_by).

claim: nativeRender calls AppInit and, only if it returns non-zero, tail-calls appRender(pauseFlag != 0).
observation: mov r4, r2; bl AppInit; cmp r0,#0; popeq; subs r0,r4,#0; movne r0,#1; pop; b appRender.
interpretation: The third JNI argument is an int flag (descriptor (I)V per docs/JNI_MAP.json), normalised to a bool before appRender.

claim: The game clock is GetTime() = System.nanoTime()/1000 (microseconds) fetched through two Java callbacks; gettimeofday is unused by the game loop.
observation: JAVATime() calls CallIntMethod for method IDs at gJAVAFunction+0x114 (JAVATime: low word) and +0x120 (JAVATimeHi: high word), combines them into a u64 and calls __aeabi_uldivmod(.., 1000). The smali shows JAVATime stores System.nanoTime() in JTime and returns the low 32 bits; JAVATimeHi returns JTime>>32.
interpretation: The clock is monotonic, in microseconds. The only gettimeofday caller is _getTime (used by the dead nativePause path).
next_step: JNI worker: confirm the smali lines and the return conversions.

claim: appRender runs a fixed-timestep update of 16666 us with catch-up capped at 4 updates per frame and at least one update per frame, then renders once.
observation: T=GetTime(); L=gTimeLast (u64). T<=L: 1 update, gTimeLast=L. L<T<=L+S: 1, L+S. <=L+2S: 2, L+2S. <=L+3S: 3, L+3S. Else 4, gTimeLast=T. S=movw #0x411a. Each update: FontAI(); cRGame::AI(Game), with G0RenderNextFlag=0 except for the last. Then G0RenderAvailable=1; G0Render(); G0RenderAvailable=0. If pause!=0 and *(Game+0x718b4)==0, it is set to 4.
interpretation: Nominal 60 Hz simulation. The simulation cannot run slower than the frame rate: at >60 fps it runs fast (likely). The first frame (L=0) runs 4 updates and resyncs.

claim: cRResourceManager::AI reloads invalidated GL resources over several frames with a 66,666 us per-frame budget.
location: v7a:0x7eb4c-0x7ed5c; budget movw/movt r9=0x1046a at v7a:0x7ec3c
observation: States: 0 idle (return 1); 1 splash->2; 2 splash + cRBackdrop::MakeVBO(Game+0x4d2e0) ->3; 3 per entry marked 1: type 0 G0TextureLoad+Remove, type 2 RShellSoundRegister, type 4 cRObjects::ReBuildObjects; time check -> splash+return 0; done ->4; 4 splash, SetSplash(''), ->0, cRLoadingBar::AI, JAVAMusicRestart. 1200 entries x 0x8c bytes.
interpretation: This is the GL context-loss recovery path, triggered by nativeReInit (ReInit sets state 1).

claim: All function addresses materialised anywhere in the image are enumerable: 42 vtable slots, 11 INIT_ARRAY entries and 3 GOT-held pointers (plus libgcc-internal tables).
location: v7a R_ARM_RELATIVE targets in .text: .data.rel.ro (42), .init_array (11), .got (3: 0x8b128 ObjectProcVertexCompare, 0x8b2a4 DatHashGetString, 0x8b2ac TexturesFunctionGetName), .text (8, libgcc)
observation: No relocated pointer in .data points into .text (634 .data->.rodata, 30 .data->.data). The capstone resolver finds exactly those 3 GOT pointers as 'address taken' (FUNCTION_INDEX address_taken_by).
interpretation: There is no function-pointer state table; indirect control flow is limited to virtual AI() dispatch, the cRHash callback, qsort's comparator and JNIEnv calls.
next_step: Also scan for pointers built with movw/movt or arithmetic (none seen in PIC code).

claim: RTTI is absent; there are 42 vtables of 12 bytes, each {0, 0, slot0}. slot0 is AI() for every class except cRGame (LevelInit(int)).
observation: No _ZTI/_ZTS symbols; typeinfo words are 0; e.g. _ZTV6cRGame slot0 = 0x2e010 cRGame::LevelInit(int); _ZTV5cRBod slot0 = 0x1cbac cRBod::AI(). cRDirectXModel/cRWorld/cRPath/cRBodPos inherit cRBod::AI.
interpretation: Consistent with -fno-rtti. There are no virtual destructors, so objects are never deleted polymorphically.

claim: cRGame::AI dispatches virtual slot 0 (AI) over the cRBod linked list at Game+0x35c and on the object at Game+0xd4.
location: v7a:0x3b12c, v7a:0x3b17c, v7a:0x3b194 (mov lr,pc; ldr pc,[r3])
observation: r3 = *(obj) (vptr); the call goes through [vptr+0]. The list is walked via obj+0xc; obj+4 holds flags: 0x10 triggers RShellError('Debug Bod AI'), and 0x40 is set on the next node during the call and cleared after (from the pseudocode, matching 0x3b118-0x3b13c).
interpretation: The target set is the 42 vtables' slot 0; which classes are live depends on the cLinkedList<cRBod>::Add calls in Init1/2/3/4.
next_step: Enumerate list insertions to narrow the per-site target sets.

claim: .bss (0x31fbdc bytes) is almost entirely covered by sized OBJECT symbols; two 1 MiB arrays dominate.
observation: 154 sized objects cover 3,275,691 of 3,275,740 bytes (49 bytes of padding). Largest: gGroup 0x106000 @0x15c6a8, gGroup0 0x106000 @0x2626a8, RShellMemory 0x2bf2c, gRSpriteManager 0x2afa4, gResourceManager 0x2904c, RMathCos/RMathSin 0x20000 each, FontPrintBuffer 0x10800.
interpretation: Static layout is fully named. The 3.8 MB cRGame lives on the heap (EV-NAT-0019), not in .bss.

claim: The v7a function inventory has 1173 unique function starts (from 1183 raw FUNC symbols): 1096 game, 18 JNI, 59 runtime; 1151 have EXIDX entries; only 8 bytes of .text are outside every symbol range.
observation: 9 same-address alias groups; 11 zero-size symbols (libgcc asm; size taken to next symbol); boundary confidence symbol+exidx 1151, symbol 11, heuristic 11. Gaps: 0x19694 and 0x4b3fc, 4 zero bytes each ($d padding). Ghidra found no function in .text lacking a symbol.
interpretation: There are no hidden or unnamed functions to recover; game-code coverage of the inventory is complete at the symbol level.

claim: The capstone call graph and Ghidra's agree on 3096 of 3099 direct/tail call edges in v7a; both see 78 unresolved indirect call sites.
observation: Only-capstone edges: 3 tail branches from single-instruction/tail functions to free@plt/glColor4f@plt, which Ghidra models as thunks. v5: 4618 common of 4621, with 3 soft-float fall-through differences on each side.
interpretation: The two independent pipelines corroborate each other; the remaining differences are modelling artefacts.

claim: Ghidra 11.4.2 decompiled every non-placeholder function in both builds without errors or timeouts (v7a 1265/1265; v5 1307/1307; timeout 60 s).
observation: v7a counts include 1173 .text functions and 92 PLT thunks (95 EXTERNAL placeholders skipped). Configuration: image base 0, $d regions pre-defined as data, TMode=0, __stdcall_softfp with explicit 'this', 4047 bogus operand references into linker metadata removed, 'Infer constant pointers' off.
interpretation: DECOMPILED says nothing about correctness. Known artefacts: 64-bit arithmetic rendered through CONCAT44, some argument lists (e.g. JNIMouseEvent) garbled, and literal-pool floats shown as hex casts.

claim: JNIKey dereferences Game without a null check, and for unmapped keycodes calls KeySet with an uninitialised register.
observation: Unmapped keycode path: ldr r3,[Game]; ldr r3,[r3,#0xbf0]; cmp #2; b 0x13e04 -> KeySet(r4) where r4 is never written in this function (callee-saved, pushed unchanged).
interpretation: Two original bugs: a crash if a key arrives before AppInit state 0, and an undefined scancode for unmapped keys when keypad mode == 2. The port must choose defined behaviour and document it.

claim: cRGame::AI keeps a float accumulator stepped by 1.0 and ticks while it exceeds 1.0, giving one inner tick per call after a one-call warm-up.
location: v7a:0x3affc-0x3b04c, loop back-edge region 0x3b0c4..; literal 1.0f at v7a:0x3b238
observation: vldr s14,[r4,#724]; vadd s15,s14,1.0; vstr; vcmpe s15, s16(1.0); ble skip; loop: s15 -= 1.0 ... while > 1.0.
interpretation: Hypothesis: the accumulator exists for time scaling elsewhere; no other writer of Game+0x2d4 has been identified yet.
next_step: Search every store to [Game+0x2d4] (xrefs cannot see heap fields; use Ghidra pseudocode).

claim: RMathInit builds 32768-entry sin/cos float tables from libm double sin()/cos(), and gRMathRand2Init loads or generates RandTable.bin with unseeded lrand48.
observation: Angle = i * 2^-15 * 2 * pi (float math), then (float)cos/sin(double). If RandTable.bin is missing, 8191 shorts come from lrand48() without srand48 (srand48 is only called from RandSeed/gRegisterInit) and the file is saved.
interpretation: Bit-exact reproduction depends on bionic libm results and the bionic lrand48 default seed (hypothesis: capture the tables from the original for validation).
next_step: Assets worker: check whether RandTable.bin is present in asm.mp3.

claim: InitGL sets the fixed GLES1 state and uploads a static quad index buffer.
observation: glGenBuffers; glBindBuffer(0x8893); glBufferData(0x8893, 0xC00, idx, 0x88E4); glEnable(0x0BD0), glEnable(0x809D), glShadeModel(0x1D00), glClearColor(0,0,0,0), glClearDepthf(1), glEnable(0x0B71), glDepthFunc(0x0203), glDepthRangef(0,1), glHint(0x0C50,0x1101), glHint(0x0C52,0x1101), glDisable(0x0BC0), glColor4f(1,1,1,1).
interpretation: GL_DITHER, GL_MULTISAMPLE, GL_FLAT, GL_DEPTH_TEST, GL_LEQUAL, GL_FASTEST hints, alpha test off; 256-quad index buffer.

claim: Touch input is ignored until boot completes and is mapped into a virtual 640-unit-wide space.
observation: ldrb gGameValid; return if 0; x * 640.0f / gG0DeviceScreenWidth; then cRMouse::ClickiPhone/ClickOn/ClickOff on Game+0x228 depending on the action.
interpretation: gGameValid is set in AppInit state 9 (0x16514).

claim: Configuration persistence: gConfig (304 B) gets compiled-in defaults, is overwritten from asm.cfg at AppInit state 2, and is saved by SetGameState and others.
observation: gRegisterLoadFile('asm.cfg', gConfig) goes PfmLoadFile -> JAVACLoadFile -> Java JAVALoadFile; gRegisterSaveFile -> PfmSaveFile -> JAVACSaveFile. OpenFeint data goes to 'of.cfg' (OFOLoad 0x7d9c0 / OFOSave 0x7d6d8).
interpretation: Save and config I/O go through Java callbacks, not native fopen (native fopen is used only by dev/export paths).

claim: v5 and v7a have the same symbol-level structure: same game/JNI function counts, the same 42 vtables and the same 254 object symbols, at different addresses.
observation: v5: 1253 raw FUNC / 1214 unique; game 1096, jni 18, runtime 100 (extra soft-float helpers); 139 nested-name scopes, 52 proven classes, 42 vtables, .bss object bytes identical (3,275,691).
interpretation: Same source, different compiler targets; per-function semantics must still be re-verified per build.

claim: JNIDatUnInit does not close the archive: it only calls the no-op wprintf twice.
observation: wprintf('JNIDatUnInit +'); wprintf('JNIDatUnInit -').
interpretation: gDatFP / gJavaAssetFid live for the life of the process.

claim: The pause flag reaches the game as an injected ESC key through an auto-quit counter at Game+0x718b4.
observation: appRender sets *(Game+0x718b4)=4 when pause!=0 and it is 0; nativeReInit sets it to 4 unconditionally. cRQuit::AI, when the counter is >0, sets it to 0 and calls KeySet(1) (pseudocode).
interpretation: KeySet(1) = DIK_ESCAPE, which opens the in-game quit/pause menu (likely; DirectInput scancode convention also seen in JNIKey).
